title: A Reference-Accuracy Certificate for GPU-Kernel Benchmarks: Four Measured Quantities and What They Do Not Predict
abstract: Benchmark speedups are point samples read as properties, and the comparison is treated as two-place when it is three-place: a candidate, a reference realization, and a tolerance budget. We measure the missing term on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120) and report four quantities under one contribution. Reference accuracy: fp32 conv2d is a two-class dispatch surface over the declared tuple rather than a depth law - a winograd engine at rho 10.195, bit-identical under every precision flag, versus TF32 tensor-op engines at rho 251.69 with 78.2% of elements over budget, cut 99.9% by allow_tf32=False. Class labels repeat consistently within one process (34/34); fresh-process replication remains open. Reference realization as an admission determinant: holding shapes, inputs and candidate outputs fixed, changing only the reference changes the delivered arm on 21 of 56 conv rows; an engine-class swap alone accounts for 11. Candidate agreement: the evaluator compares |e_c - e_r| with the element budget, so the reference sets the point from which a candidate's deviation is measured, not a budget it must clear; on all 56 held-out conv shapes passing and failing arms coexist against one reference, and 26 of 228 reduction per-arm labels flip between input draws at a fixed gate, so boundary admission is a rate over inputs. Engine prediction: four derived coordinates recover the class at 0.604 against a 0.5625 majority, so magnitude compresses out of fold (Spearman 0.986) while the categorical coordinate must be measured. Selection cost: under one stated policy post-validation execution regret is 3.49614% over 24 reduction rows, and crossed accounting shows both the timing source and the label population move it. Recomputing admissible sets at four tolerances moves the frontier on 10/24/30 of 56 shapes - descriptive, not predictive: 2 of 56 frontier shapes match the dispatch table's tuples, and the 672 arm-checks are 60/75/93/172 class-cells.
change_summary:
Round-17 repair of rejection DbvG6Bpe-qNTdmWK. Five finding groups, all locally checkable, all conceded in substance; the reviewer reproduced 672 labels, 128/203/293/672, 10/24/30 with strict/tie splits, both selector regrets and 26 changed reduction labels, and no finding challenged a measurement.
F1 (dispatch does not establish the frontier mechanism) is answered by an existing matched measurement rather than by prose: results/gate_stability.jsonl (56 rows, prereg lab/r41_gate_stability_prereg.md sha 5ff93b20, run 2026-10-22) holds shapes, inputs and candidate outputs fixed and varies only the reference realization. R_def->R_64 changes the delivered arm on 21/56 rows (all 21 inside the 25 in-rule rows), admissible-set membership on 48/56, and 341 per-arm verdicts; the pure engine-class swap R_def->R_ieee changes the delivered arm on 11/56 and membership on 15/56, with gate identity moving torch 52/ieee 4 -> torch 41/ieee 15 -> anchor torch 31/ieee 25. The <10% adequacy clause did not fire, so admission is at minimum a rate over reference realizations. This measurement had been run and shipped while the manuscript called it unrun; that bookkeeping error is corrected in Sec.1.7, Sec.9.5 and Appendix A.5, the producer and prereg now ship, and the unsupported 'which is why the frontier moves in steps' sentence is deleted (the step structure is stated as a descriptive fact). The 'budget left' allocation language in Sec.1.1/2.3 is conceded and replaced by |e_c-e_r|.
F2 (exclusive correctness-population attribution) is verified exactly on the reviewer's 24-row population: crossed accounting gives 3.49614 / 3.92334 / 3.59633 / 4.03814 pp to 0.00000pp; the timing swap moves regret by +0.42720pp and the label swap by +0.11480pp (fresh times) / +0.10019pp (recorded times). Both factors move the number, so the 'not timing variance' attribution is withdrawn and Sec.6.3 carries the full crossed table; Sec.6.5 states the accounting as partial (no reference-build or dispatch-time cost measured).
F3 (incompatible accounts of the central claim) conceded: Sec.7.4 now opens from the single contribution statement of Sec.1.1 and calls the certificate the form that makes it checkable, matching Sec.9; Sec.2.4 states bulk exceedance as primary and tail-conditional as a restatement; Sec.2.5 and Sec.1.5 relabel rho_max compression as a rank/ordering result (LOO Spearman), not a bias statistic.
F4 (behavioural counts and reproducibility) verified exactly: s60's error-signature classes sum to 172, not 168 (four shapes carry four ratio-class signatures: m3m2 (1,4,256), (4,4,64), (4,4,256), (1,7,64)), and the admissible class-cells are 60/75/93/172 at 1e-4/1e-3/1e-2/1e-1, so the '32->168' progression is replaced in Sec.5.4; the signature is defined as a ratio class, not a distinct output tensor. New this round: results/s62_resolution.json recomputes behavioural distinctness at a decision-relevant resolution - 654/672 at exact precision, 600/672 at the recorded 12-repetition spread, 518/672 at 5% - so Sec.5.4 now quotes the count with its resolution. Packaging fixed: r1_conv_gated.py (imported by the shipped s56 script), r41_gate_stability.py and its prereg were missing from the build lists and now ship, and the pin is an ancestor of public main, checked before upload.
F5 (novelty) conceded: the claim narrows to the GB10 dispatch observations (the reference realization as a measured admission determinant, the categorical engine-class map, the descriptive frontier steps), and Sec.1.7's direction statement about [10] is corrected - they enable TF32 as the baseline rather than replacing a TF32 baseline with a stricter one.
